metadata.title: ACE Omni Accessibility Assurance Component Definition — Experimental
metadata.remarks: Experimental OSCAL Component Definition describing how the Omni assurance execution path can support the AX accessibility-assurance controls. It makes no claim that Omni itself satisfies the technical accessibility requirements of a system under assessment.

components.title: ACE Omni Accessibility Assurance Execution
components.description: A deterministic assurance execution component that binds accessibility control claims to assessment work, evidence provenance, findings, remediation state, and replayable causal traces using OSCAL as the governing compliance model.
components.purpose: Execute and evidence accessibility assurance workflows without introducing a parallel accessibility compliance schema.

control-implementations.description: Implementation claims against the experimental Federal ICT Accessibility Assurance Profile.

implemented-requirements.description: Omni can preserve an explicit, versioned assessment scope and the authoritative control identifiers selected for a run so applicability decisions are visible inputs rather than implicit assumptions.
Omni binds control identifiers to implementation claims, assessment work, observations, and evidence so control state can be traced across the assurance graph.

Omni records deterministic execution inputs, tool or adapter provenance, observations, evidence references, and replay information so accessibility assessment evidence can be reproduced and inspected.

Omni preserves the causal path from observation to finding to remediation work while OSCAL Assessment Results and POA&M remain the governing models for reportable findings, risks, dispositions, and milestones.
Omni can rerun pinned assessment definitions after scheduled or material-change triggers and distinguish fresh evidence from superseded evidence through immutable versions and provenance.
